name: UIEdgeGlow
src_typeComment: Animated "electric/flame" edge glow for item frames, achievement icons, and rarity borders — a separate, more elaborate tool from UILightingEffect's Rim mode (which stays the simple, cheap, static edge-light it already is, for buttons/panels). Drop on any UI Graphic (Image, RawImage, ...) and pick a shape; the jagged/organic look comes from the scrolling, rotating noise mask, not the edge falloff itself, which is just a plain distance-to-edge band.

src_serialized.name: glowColor
src_serialized.header: Colour (Flame uses its own gradient below instead)

src_serialized.name: hueShiftSpeed
src_serialized.tooltip: Cycles per second the glow colour rotates through the hue wheel. 0 = a static colour.

src_serialized.name: pattern
src_serialized.tooltip: WHAT the mask looks like — each pattern computes the mask itself differently (not just a re-tint of the same noise). Fluid: a thin traced line wobbling via smooth domain-warped noise. Flow: the same domain-warp technique, but as a soft blobby alpha modulation instead of a thin line. Electric: a procedural angular zigzag (lightning), not static. Flame: dominant upward scroll with its own base→tip colour gradient below.

src_serialized.name: chaseModeEnabled
src_serialized.header: Chase — an orthogonal TOGGLE, not a pattern: restricts whichever pattern above is active to a travelling comet + fading trail

src_serialized.name: chaseSpeedVariation
src_serialized.tooltip: 0 = perfectly constant speed. Above 0 adds a surging/non-uniform feel to the travel instead of linear motion.

src_serialized.name: chaseTrailLength
src_serialized.tooltip: Fraction of the full perimeter the fading trail covers behind each travelling point.

src_serialized.name: chaseInstanceCount
src_serialized.tooltip: How many comets travel the perimeter at once, evenly spaced. Overlapping trails take the brightest, never summed, so more instances can't blow out the exposure.

src_serialized.name: glowCoreWidth
src_serialized.tooltip: Fraction of Edge Width used for a tight bright inner core, on top of the normal mid band.
src_serialized.header: Glow — shared 3-layer bloom (core + mid + soft outer bleed), applies to every pattern

src_serialized.name: glowBloomWidth
src_serialized.tooltip: How many multiples of Edge Width the soft outer bloom reaches — this is what gives a genuine light-bleed feel instead of a hard-edged gradient.

src_serialized.name: fluidWarpFrequency
src_serialized.header: Fluid — a THIN traced line (not a filled band) wobbling via smooth domain-warped noise

src_serialized.name: fluidDisplacementStrength
src_serialized.tooltip: How far the traced line wobbles in/out from the true edge. Kept modest relative to Edge Width so it reads as a flowing line hugging the boundary, not a solid shape reaching into the icon.

src_serialized.name: electricDisplacementStrength
src_serialized.tooltip: How far the traced line wobbles in/out from the true edge. Kept SMALL relative to Edge Width — a large value here is what used to make Electric read as spikes shooting inward instead of a thin line hugging the boundary.
src_serialized.header: Electric — perimeter-jittered jagged path (chain lightning ALONG the edge) + stepped flicker

src_serialized.name: electricEdgeFrequency
src_serialized.tooltip: Sampled along the PERIMETER (one texture row), not in 2D UV space — this is what gives a fine erratic zigzag travelling with the edge's own direction, instead of broad 2D waves. How many jitter cycles occur across one full trip around the border.

src_serialized.name: electricInwardFadeAmount
src_serialized.tooltip: Keeps the jagged CORE line the dominant feature over the softer inward bleed (still present, just secondary) — 1 = equal weight, lower = edge pattern dominates.

src_serialized.name: electricUseRawTexture
src_serialized.tooltip: On: samples the Noise Mask directly (bright = displaced) so a hand-authored crackle texture drives the jitter as-is. Off (default): assumes raw unshaped noise and applies a ridge transform automatically.

src_serialized.name: flameDisplacementStrength
src_serialized.header: Flame — its own colour gradient, base to tip (a solid filled push, not a thin line)

src_serialized.name: noiseMask
src_serialized.tooltip: Leave empty to auto-generate a turbulent noise mask.
src_serialized.header: Edge Noise Mask — this is what gives the glow its jagged/organic look, not the edge falloff

src_serialized.name: radialUVPower
src_serialized.tooltip: Pulls the mask sample toward/away from the centre based on distance, giving it a swirl instead of a flat scroll.

src_members.name: ApplySettings
src_members.comment: Public so a self-test (or a runtime UI system) can push a settings change without waiting for OnValidate. The glow itself animates purely via the shader's own _Time.y — this does NOT need to be called every frame, only when a setting actually changes.
